title: Northwind Telemetry — on-prem architecture proposal and terraform recommendations (WIP)
body:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working proposal for Northwind Telemetry's first on-prem private deployment of Redwood Inference. Goal: provide a production-ready architecture, conservative initial sizing for inference workloads, Terraform module recommendations, and an upgrade/cutover playbook. This doc is intentionally informal — meant to capture decisions and open questions for the NW infra + platform teams.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Initial target: support 5 production services calling text-generation + embeddings with a 99th percentile latency SLO of 300ms for short requests (<= 256 tokens) and throughput of ~1800 token/sec sustained across the fleet.
- Suggested hardware: mixed H100 for burst-critical models (2 nodes) + A10G for steady-state inference (6 nodes) in the first phase.
- Storage: fast local NVMe for model cache (2TB per GPU node) + central NFS-like object store for checkpoints (S3-compatible on-prem).
- Networking: routed VPC with 25GbE connectivity between GPU hosts and control plane, separate management network for KMS/HSM traffic.
- Terraform strategy: split into 3 modules (landing-zone, compute-pool, ops-integrations). Keep minimal mutable infra for easier upgrades.

Workload assumptions and math (how we sized):
- Typical model: 7B-ish quantized variant, ~2–4 tokens per millisecond on A10G (steady), ~8–12 tokens/ms on H100 (burst).
- Peak concurrent requests: estimates from NW product indicate 200 concurrent short requests (avg 50 tokens).
- Token/sec target: 200 concurrent * 50 tokens * 0.18 RPS per user ~1800 tokens/sec (sustained). Allow 3x headroom for bursts / future growth => target capacity ~5400 tokens/sec.
- Node capacity (conservative): A10G node (1 GPU) ~600 tokens/sec sustained; H100 (~1 GPU) ~1800 tokens/sec sustained. So baseline fleet: 6 A10G + 2 H100 (gives 6*600 + 2*1800 = 7800 tokens/sec).
- Memory & KV cache: plan for 64GB RAM per GPU node; model KV cache pinned to GPU memory and small persistent LRU on NVMe.

Hardware & placement notes:
- GPU choices: recommend single-GPU shapes initially (easier TF stateful upgrades). Use A10G nodes for cost-stable workloads; H100 nodes reserved for models with long context/bigger throughput needs.
- Local storage: configure NVMe for model shards and KV cache. Minimum sizing: 2TB NVMe per node.
- Central object store: Ceph or MinIO for artifacts and model checkpoints, with 3x replication across their data center racks.
- KMS: Northwind requires HSM-backed keys. Integration path: Redwood control-plane (private) will call their on-prem YubiHSM via a bastion on management network. We should provide a KMS module (see Terraform notes) that wires HSM endpoints and mTLS certs.

Network & security constraints:
- Air-gap mode: NW will require an option to run with restricted egress. Control-plane bi-directional requirement: only outgoing TLS on port 443 to specific Red control-plane endpoints (allowlist). Draft fallback: if no egress, we ship an offline control-plane bundle + cadence updates via signed artifacts on a USB-sanitized offline device.
- Internal segmentation: inference traffic in a high-throughput subnet, control/ops in management VLAN. KMS traffic on isolated VLAN with ACLs restricting access to Redwood control-plane bastions.

Terraform module recommendations (naming + contract):
- module: nw-landing-zone
  - purpose: base network, DNS, IGW, routing, peering to customer VPCs, subnets for gpu/management/kms
  - inputs: cidr_blocks, az_map, mgmt_admins, dns_zone
  - outputs: subnet_ids, route_table_ids, mgmt_bastion_ip

- module: nw-compute-pool
  - purpose: create GPU instances, local NVMe attachments, instance profiles, taints/labels for k8s (if using k8s), autoscaling group config
  - inputs: gpu_type, gpu_count, instance_type, model_cache_size_gb, disk_iops
  - outputs: node_ids, ssh_jump_ips, node_role_arn

- module: nw-ops-integrations
  - purpose: monitoring, logging, kms wiring, alerting, TF-managed HSM credentials (read-only references), prometheus remote_write config
  - inputs: monitoring_endpoint, kms_endpoint, log_retention_days
  - outputs: grafana_url, log_bucket_name

Notes on mutable vs immutable infra:
- Prefer immutable model for compute-pool (rebuild nodes for major GPU driver updates) to minimize drift. Use AMI baking pipelines.
- Keep KMS/HSM resources as stable outputs referenced by Redwood operator.

Upgrade & cutover playbook (high level):
1) Pre-cutover checks (2 weeks before): validate network ACLs, perform simulated cold-starts in staging, verify KMS auth flow, sanity-check S3-compatible object store performance (read latency < 30ms).
2) Fleet bake (1 week): deploy A10G nodes first, run canary model, verify cost/throughput, then add H100 nodes behind routing policy labeled "burst".
3) Traffic routing: start with 5% traffic shift to on-prem, monitor latency/errs for 48 hours, then 20%, 50%, 100% with rollback windows at each step. Use Canary + gradual rollout inside Redwood Console (A/B name: northwind-cutover-2024).
4) Post-cutover: run full regression eval suite on sampleset, enable quality-monitoring alerts (threshold: drop in Rouge/embedding cosine > 0.03 triggers pager).
5) Upgrade path for minor runtime patches: in-place rolling restarts of subsets of nodes with pre-baked AMI. Major driver/kernel upgrades: full rebuild with traffic draining.

Rollback criteria & steps:
- Immediate rollback if 99th latency > 2x baseline or error rate > 1% sustained for 10 minutes.
- Rollback by shifting traffic back to hosted fallback pool (retain a warm hosted capacity per contract). If hosted fallback unavailable, scale down new nodes and re-instantiate previous AMI nodes.

Operational runbook snippets (quick):
- Draining node: /opt/redwood/bin/drain-node --node <id> --timeout 600
- Model cache clear: /opt/redwood/bin/clear-model-cache --path /nvme/cache --confirm
- Force rollback of TF-managed ASG: terraform apply -target=module.nw-compute-pool.aws_autoscaling_group.old

Open questions / risks (items to resolve before final proposal):
- HSM network requirement clarification: can YubiHSM be exposed over TLS on management subnet or must HSM be physically tied to a network appliance? (NW security team)
- Expected long-context requests: product team to confirm percentage of >2048-token calls — this affects H100 sizing.
- Backup cadence for local NVMe model caches: nightly snapshot to central object store recommended, confirm RPO with NW.
- Egress policy: confirm allowlist for Redwood control-plane IPs and maintenance windows for signed artifact updates in air-gapped mode.

Action items / owners (short):
- Confirm HSM network model with NW security — Owner: Priya — due 2024-10-15
- Run model perf microbench on NW sample prompts (A10G vs H100) — Owner: Diego — due 2024-10-18
- Draft Terraform module skeleton and publish PR — Owner: Riley — due 2024-10-22 (linked PR above)

Appendix: quick Terraform variable example for nw-compute-pool (conceptual):
- variable "gpu_type" { default = "A10G" }
- variable "gpu_count" { default = "6" }
- variable "model_cache_size_gb" { default = "2048" }
- resource tags: { Project = "northwind-telemetry", Owner = "NW-Platform" }

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep upgrade steps minimal; customers hate long cutovers. Consider a cold-warm design for H100 nodes so large-context models don't block short requests.
- Add a small runbook for data retention/regulatory requirements (NW has 7-year retention on logs).

References and links:
- internal perf harness: github.com/redwood-inference/inference-bench (see perf/northwind)
- reference terraform modules: github.com/redwood-inference/infra-templates/tree/main/modules/gpu

End of draft.

-- Riley
